claims.statement: Classify the decision-review standing repair as a technical integrity repair, not a methodological adaptation, and do not claim a new learned method from it.

attributes.decision: Should the decision-review standing repair be classified as a methodological adaptation or a technical integrity repair?
attributes.basis: The repair changed how a producer validates an assessment reference at the review source revision. That is a validation-integrity change. It did not demonstrate a changed reusable reasoning procedure, so the adaptation-object check does not support a methodological-development claim.
attributes.conditions: Applies when a consequential technical repair is offered as evidence of methodological development or a new learned method.
attributes.counterevidence: The repair yielded a reusable validation principle: derive effective standing with the existing consumer at the exact source revision. That principle is a technical rule; no before/after intellectual procedure was observed.
attributes.claim_ceiling: One same-agent classification. It does not establish independent reuse, decision influence, comparative benefit, longitudinal development or promotion of a method.
